channel.title: VIA Chart Guides
channel.description: Educational chart and data visualization guides from VIA.

item.title: Pie Chart vs Bar Chart
item.description: Use a pie chart for parts of one whole with few categories. Use a bar chart to compare magnitudes across categories, especially when labels are many or values are close.

item.title: Bar Chart vs Line Chart
item.description: Use bars for discrete category comparison. Use lines when values are ordered—usually over time—and you care about direction and rate of change.

item.title: Line Chart vs Area Chart
item.description: Both show trends. A line emphasizes path and slope; an area chart fills under the line to emphasize magnitude and volume of change.

item.title: Bar Chart vs Horizontal Bar Chart
item.description: Vertical bars are familiar for short labels. Horizontal bars (H. Bar in VIA) win when category names are long or you want an easy ranked list.

item.title: Pie Chart vs Donut Chart
item.description: They encode the same part-to-whole data. A donut opens the center for a total or label; choose based on layout, not a different analysis.

item.title: Radar Chart vs Bar Chart
item.description: Radar shows a multi-attribute profile as a shape. Bars rank magnitudes clearly. Prefer bars for precise comparison; radar for holistic profile shape.
